original_abstract.text: Hybrid language models keep a key-value (KV) cache only in their few full-attention layers, but this cache is still the part of a prompt's state that grows with the prompt and that must be stored or moved to reuse it. We present DCKV, a differentiable codec for the KV cache and the first KV-cache codec that is trained end to end. Its transform, its quantizer and its entropy models, which are conditioned on the prompt tokens and on already decoded neighbouring positions, are optimized together against the frozen language model, both for the code length that the entropy models assign and for the change of the model's output. On Qwen3.5-2B, DCKV stores a compressed token in more than 55 times fewer bytes than bf16 at a loss of at most 1.8 points on three long-context benchmarks, and in more than 100 times fewer bytes at a loss of at most 3.6 points.
original_abstract.source_title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models

en.text: DCKV jointly trains a transform, quantizer and conditional entropy model to compress the prompt KV cache against a frozen hybrid language model. On Qwen3.5-2B it reports over 55× fewer bytes per compressed token with at most 1.8-point loss on three long-context benchmarks, or over 100× compression with at most 3.6-point loss.

zh.text: DCKV面向冻结的混合语言模型，联合训练变换、量化器和条件熵模型来压缩提示词KV缓存。在Qwen3.5-2B的三个长上下文基准上，每个压缩token的字节数减少超过55倍时损失最多1.8个百分点，减少超过100倍时损失最多3.6个百分点。

original_abstract.text: A user history can admit multiple plausible next interactions, yet conventional sequential recommenders produce a single deterministic ranking. While diffusion models offer a natural way to sample alternative continuations, we show that existing target-item diffusion recommenders often suffer from severe sampling collapse, producing nearly identical outputs across independent draws. We identify two ubiquitous design choices that promote this collapse: joint learning of the latent space and denoiser, and in-trajectory supervision via discrete losses. To address these failure modes, we introduce DARTS (Diverse and Accurate Recommendation Through Sampling), a three-stage latent diffusion framework that explicitly decouples representation learning, generative modeling, and discrete ranking by learning and freezing the latent space before diffusion training and postponing ranking supervision to the final decoding stage. We further characterize sampling diversity using complementary measures of variation before and after decoding, and use posterior-predictive aggregation to exploit this diversity at inference. Across three Amazon Reviews 2023 categories, DARTS preserves substantially greater sampling diversity while outperforming strong sequential, generative-retrieval, and diffusion baselines by 7-12% on standard ranking metrics. Aggregating multiple samples further improves ranking accuracy at a fixed slate size.
original_abstract.source_title: When Diffusion Recommenders Stop Sampling: Preserving Generative Diversity

en.text: DARTS separates representation learning, diffusion modeling, and discrete ranking to preserve alternative next-item samples. It freezes the latent space before diffusion training and postpones ranking supervision until decoding, addressing collapse associated with jointly learning representations and the denoiser or applying discrete losses inside denoising trajectories. On three Amazon Reviews 2023 categories, it reports greater sampling diversity and stronger ranking metrics than evaluated baselines. Aggregating several samples further improves ranking at a fixed slate size, suggesting a recommendation-specific way to use additional inference compute.

zh.text: DARTS 将表示学习、扩散建模和离散排序分开：先冻结潜在空间，再训练扩散模型，把排序监督延后到最终解码，缓解多次采样仍生成近乎相同结果的问题。在 Amazon Reviews 2023 的三个类别中，作者报告采样多样性和排序指标均优于所比较的基线。最终推荐列表大小固定时，聚合多个样本还能改善排序，为生成式推荐增加推理计算提供了一条具体路径。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval models have been increasingly adopted in search and recommendation systems. However, industrial generative retrieval models are commonly specialized to a fixed online scenario: they learn from scenario-specific interactions, support a narrow set of query forms and retrieval objectives. We study how to remove these couplings and build a unified end-to-end multimodal search system for open-ended image--text queries, heterogeneous shopping intents, and online scenarios with different resource constraints. We present \textbf{PailitaoMMSearch}, which directly generates product Semantic IDs from a raw query image and free-form instruction and scales along three dimensions. \textbf{Data scaling} uses a reusable toolset that can be composed into intent- and lifecycle-specific workflows for cold-start synthesis, quality control, real-traffic refinement, and continuous data production. \textbf{Intent scaling} progressively equips one model with e-commerce product knowledge, multiple retrieval relations, and adjustable reasoning budgets through continual pre-training (CPT), mixed-budget supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and unified reinforcement learning (RL). The RL stage combines intent-balanced optimization and Sample--Beam rollouts aligned with multi-candidate serving. \textbf{Scenario scaling} exposes quality--cost operating points across model capacity and reasoning budget. The system is deployed in multimodal search applications on Taobao Pailitao. A controlled online A/B test reports statistically significant improvements, including item page views $\textbf{+17.90\%}$, transactions $\textbf{+27.04\%}$, and gross merchandise value $\textbf{+8.94\%}$.
original_abstract.source_title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search

en.text: PailitaoMMSearch directly generates product semantic IDs from images and free-form instructions. It scales data workflows, shopping intents and deployment scenarios through continual pretraining, mixed-budget supervised fine-tuning and intent-balanced reinforcement learning with serving-aligned rollouts. A controlled online A/B test on Taobao Pailitao reports statistically significant gains of 17.90% in item page views, 27.04% in transactions and 8.94% in gross merchandise value.

zh.text: PailitaoMMSearch 从图像和自由文本指令直接生成商品语义 ID，通过持续预训练、混合推理预算监督微调，以及兼顾意图平衡和服务端多候选生成的强化学习，扩展数据生产、购物意图和部署场景。淘宝拍立淘的受控线上 A/B 测试报告商品浏览量、交易量和成交总额分别显著提升 17.90%、27.04% 和 8.94%。

original_abstract.text:
Coordinating multiple recommendation objectives (e.g., click and conversion) is critical for real-world generative recommendation (GR). However, since a positive item in GR can be retrieved only when its tokens are successively selected at every decoding step, traditional item-wise methods lack fine-grained token-wise supervision to guide intermediate steps. Motivated by its success in foundation models, we consider introducing multi-objective on-policy distillation (MOPD) into GR to distill two single-objective teachers into a student at each token. Yet, we find that in vanilla MOPD, (i) teachers exhibit unequal distillation difficulty at each token (i.e., token-level imbalance), and (ii) the harder-to-distill teacher varies across tokens (i.e., cross-token inconsistency), leaving each objective poorly learned at certain steps and hindering positive item retrieval for both objectives, leading to suboptimal performance.
To address this challenge, we propose KL-MOPD (KL-Weighted Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation), a simple yet effective distillation method that allocates token-wise teacher weights proportional to the initial student-teacher token-wise KL divergences, thereby strengthening supervision for the harder-to-distill teacher at every decoding step. Despite its simplicity, we theoretically prove that KL-MOPD strictly outperforms vanilla MOPD in the additive joint recommendation objective under mild conditions. Moreover, KL-MOPD is plug-and-play and computationally efficient, requiring only a one-time pre-training weight calibration with negligible training overhead. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks, a billion-scale industrial dataset, and online A/B tests on our e-commerce advertising platform demonstrate that KL-MOPD significantly improves both individual and joint recommendation performance. The anonymous code is provided for peer review.
original_abstract.source_title: KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation

en.text: KL-MOPD distills single-objective teachers into a multi-objective generative recommender, weighting each teacher at each token by the initial student-teacher KL divergence. This prioritizes harder-to-distill objectives with one-time calibration and negligible training overhead. The paper proves improvement over vanilla multi-objective on-policy distillation under stated mild conditions and reports individual and joint objective gains on public benchmarks, a billion-scale industrial dataset and online advertising tests.

zh.text: KL-MOPD 将单目标教师蒸馏到多目标生成式推荐学生中，按初始学生与教师的 token 级 KL 散度分配权重，增强较难蒸馏目标的监督；仅需一次校准，训练额外开销很小。论文在所述温和条件下证明其优于普通多目标在策略蒸馏，并在公开基准、十亿级工业数据和线上广告测试中报告单目标与联合目标收益。

original_abstract.text: Next-item prediction is inherently ambiguous: a single interaction history often admits multiple plausible continuations across distinct catalogue regions. Standard sequential recommenders compress these alternatives into a single prediction, conflating user intents. We introduce COllapse-resistant Multiple hyPOThesis lEarning (COMPOTE), a multi-hypothesis transformer trained with an annealed objective that transitions from uniform supervision to a winner-takes-all assignment. This mechanism forces hypotheses to specialize into distinct catalogue regions, while inference relies on an efficient, normalizer-free max-similarity rule. Theoretically, we show that in the population case, the optimal solutions partition the conditional next-item distribution according to a max-entropy quantization principle, while pooled scores preserve the Bayes-optimal ranking. We also prove a generalization bound scaling logarithmically with the number of hypotheses. Across three Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmarks, COMPOTE outperforms strong ID-based, generative, and multi-interest baselines using item IDs alone. Matched-capacity ablations confirm that performance gains stem directly from the annealed objective, preventing the head collapse observed in conventional multi-head architectures, rather than added capacity, ensembling, or routing.
original_abstract.source_title: Compote: Collapse-Resistant Multiple Hypothesis Learning For Sequential Recommendation

en.text: COMPOTE represents several plausible next-item continuations with a multi-hypothesis Transformer. An annealed objective moves from uniform supervision to winner-takes-all assignments so hypotheses specialize, while inference uses a normalizer-free maximum-similarity rule. Across three Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmarks, it outperforms evaluated ID-based, generative, and multi-interest baselines; matched-capacity ablations attribute the gains to the training objective rather than added capacity. It offers a way to reduce head collapse in multi-interest modeling, but does not establish a long-history or model-size scaling law.

zh.text: COMPOTE 用多个假设表示同一段历史可能对应的不同下一物品意图，训练目标从均匀监督逐步转向赢家负责，促使不同假设形成分工；推理采用无需归一化的最大相似度打分。在 Amazon Reviews 2023 的三个基准中，作者报告优于所比较的 ID、生成式和多兴趣方法，等容量消融将收益归于训练目标，而非增加参数。可借鉴的是减少多兴趣表示中的预测头坍塌，论文未建立长历史或模型规模的 scaling law。

original_abstract.text: Embedding-level scaling expands the capacity of language models through lookup-based memory rather than by increasing model depth, width, or dense computation. Extending this idea to vision-language models (VLMs) is challenging because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. We introduce V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for VLMs. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, and modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals; all addressing is non-parametric, and the retrieved embeddings are fused into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks, V-LUMEN substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. At a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating that external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method. Because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Code is available at https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen.
original_abstract.source_title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models

en.text: V-LUMEN expands vision-language capacity with a lookup table instead of additional dense per-token computation. A frozen codebook discretizes visual features; spatial hashing and text-conditioned relevance address memory, whose embeddings enter the backbone through gated residuals. Tests on five reasoning benchmarks and three disjoint-image transfer benchmarks support this capacity axis; matched-budget LoRA/MoE comparisons preserve accuracy on two backbones. Lookup occurs once at prefill and is constant in table size.

zh.text: V-LUMEN将视觉特征经固定码本离散化，用空间哈希和文本相关性寻址外部记忆，再通过门控残差接入视觉语言模型，以存储扩容代替增加逐token稠密计算。五个推理基准和三个图像不重叠的迁移基准验证了这条容量扩展路径；在两个骨干上，将部分LoRA或MoE容量转入记忆仍能保持准确率。查表仅发生在预填充阶段，其成本不随表大小增长。

original_abstract.text: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language-model training can exhibit large loss spikes with Muon-family optimizers. We introduce EnergyCal, a lightweight rule that attenuates routed-expert updates according to the normalized squared Frobenius norm of their finite-step Newton-Schulz directions. EnergyCal leaves the spectral transform unchanged and adds no persistent optimizer state. We evaluate it on a 4B-parameter MoE model. Against a development-selected, lower-learning-rate MuonH recipe, EnergyCal-MuonH reduces mean thresholded loss-spike burden by 99.51% and final geometric-mean perplexity by 4.06%, with a modest throughput cost. With plain Muon at matched nominal learning rate and weight decay, the reduction in mean spike burden averages 95.98% across the two tested exponents, accompanied by small endpoint improvements. These findings support stabilization both with and without Hyperball in the evaluated setting.
original_abstract.source_title: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training

en.text: EnergyCal attenuates routed-expert updates using normalized squared Frobenius norms of finite-step Newton-Schulz directions, leaving the spectral transform unchanged and adding no persistent optimizer state. On a 4B-parameter sparse MoE, it reduces mean thresholded loss-spike burden by 99.51% and final geometric-mean perplexity by 4.06% relative to a selected lower-learning-rate MuonH recipe, with modest throughput cost. Plain-Muon experiments also show stabilization within the evaluated settings.

zh.text: EnergyCal 按有限步 Newton-Schulz 更新方向的归一化 Frobenius 范数平方衰减路由专家更新，不改变谱变换，也不增加持久优化器状态。在 40 亿参数稀疏 MoE 上，相对经开发选择的较低学习率 MuonH 配方，阈值化损失尖峰负担均值下降 99.51%，最终几何平均困惑度下降 4.06%，吞吐代价适中。普通 Muon 实验也在所评测设定下显示稳定性收益。

original_abstract.text: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction relies on historical behaviors and contextual features to estimate clicks on a target item. Existing Transformer-based CTR models often adopt index-based or temporal positional encodings and token-level causal interaction. However, we observe that most existing positional encodings do not outperform NoPE, while relaxing causal constraints within target-relative temporal groups also yields gains. These observations motivate a fundamental question: what positional encoding and interaction granularity does CTR prediction actually require? To address this question, we propose \textbf{TRIP}, which combines target-aware rank--time positional encoding with temporal-group interaction modeling. Specifically, Factorized Rank Encoding represents each behavior's ordinal position within the historical sequence through a low-rank factorization, while Target-Relative Time Encoding characterizes its temporal distance to the target on a coarse-to-fine scale. This joint design grounds each behavior's positional representation in its sequence context and temporal relation to the current target. Furthermore, Temporal Group-Causal Interaction enriches intra-group representations through bidirectional interaction and masked reconstruction while preserving inter-group causal order. Finally, behavior representations are condensed into compact group summaries for efficient group-level modeling in subsequent layers. Experiments on four public benchmarks show that TRIP improves AUC by up to 4.45\% relative to the strongest baseline.
original_abstract.source_title: Rethinking Positional Encoding and Interaction Granularity for CTR Prediction

en.text: TRIP combines factorized rank encoding and target-relative time encoding with temporal-group interactions for CTR prediction. Bidirectional interaction and masked reconstruction operate within groups while causal order is preserved between groups; compact group summaries support efficient later-layer modeling. On four public benchmarks, the authors report up to 4.45% relative AUC improvement over the strongest baseline.

zh.text: TRIP 将低秩分解的序位编码、目标相对时间编码与时间分组交互结合，用于 CTR 预测。组内采用双向交互和掩码重建，组间保留因果顺序，并以紧凑的分组摘要降低后续层建模开销。在四个公开基准上，作者报告相对最强基线最高 4.45% 的 AUC 提升。

original_abstract.text: Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexes, such as HNSW, are the backbone of modern vector search. However, their massive memory footprint creates a severe infrastructure bottleneck. While vector quantization is widely adopted to reduce the memory required to store data vectors, the graph's edge structure increasingly dominates total memory usage. Compressing these adjacency lists for online search presents a critical system challenge: because decompression occurs during query processing, i.e., while navigating the graph, memory savings cannot come at the expense of query latency. In this paper, we present a compression technique explicitly tailored for live HNSW routing. By applying offline graph permutations to artificially induce structural locality, we enable the use of SIMD-accelerated integer compressors, such as Stream VByte, for rapid on-the-fly decompression. Evaluated across diverse real-world workloads, we significantly outperform the current state of the art in both compression ratio and query latency. Our experimental results show that we achieve compression ratios up to 52.7% with negligible penalties in latency compared to the uncompressed baseline. Furthermore, our technique has been effectively deployed in production at eBay, achieving up to 44.3% reduction in edge storage with no degradation in query latency.
original_abstract.source_title: Lossless Compression of Proximity Graph Indexes for Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search

en.text: This work reduces HNSW graph-edge storage by permuting nodes offline to create locality and applying SIMD-accelerated integer compression during online traversal. It reports compression ratios up to 52.7% with negligible latency penalties; an eBay deployment reduces edge storage by up to 44.3% without query-latency degradation. The savings concern graph edges rather than the entire retrieval service.

zh.text: 该研究通过离线重排节点增强邻接表局部性，再以SIMD整数压缩支持查询时快速解码，减少HNSW图边的内存开销。实验报告最高52.7%的压缩比例且延迟代价很小；eBay生产部署中，边存储最多减少44.3%，查询延迟未退化。这里的节省针对图边，而非整个检索服务。

original_abstract.text: Semantic ID-based recommendation represents each item as a sequence of semantic tokens obtained through residual quantization. This paradigm generates the next item's tokens autoregressively from coarse to fine, entailing each prediction attending to historical tokens at all semantic levels. However, our inference-time analysis reveals that historical tokens at the target-token's semantic level tend to be more informative, whereas other levels can introduce interference. Motivated by these findings, we propose LESSRec that separately encodes the historical token sequence at each semantic level and restricts attention over historical tokens to the sequence at the target token's semantic level during prediction. To complement these level-specific histories, LESSRec explicitly provides an item-level semantic sequence that represents each historical item's overall semantics in chronological order. The decoder accesses the level-aligned token sequence and the item-level semantic sequence through two separate cross-attention branches and fuses their contexts. We further introduce LESSRec+, which uses separate encoders for different semantic-level histories with the same total parameter count to reduce encoder computation. Extensive experiments across three public datasets and three tokenizers demonstrate the recommendation effectiveness of LESSRec and LESSRec+, with efficiency analyses highlighting the computational benefits of LESSRec+.
original_abstract.source_title: LESSRec: Level-Specific History Modeling for Semantic ID-Based Recommendation

en.text: LESSRec encodes semantic-ID history separately by quantization level and restricts historical token attention to the target level. A second cross-attention branch accesses chronological item-level semantics to complement the level-specific context. LESSRec+ uses separate level encoders at the same total parameter count to reduce encoder computation. Three datasets and three tokenizers support recommendation effectiveness and the computational benefits of LESSRec+.

zh.text: LESSRec 按语义 ID 的量化层级分别编码历史，并让目标 token 只关注同层级的历史 token；另一交叉注意力分支读取按时间排列的物品级语义，补充层级上下文。LESSRec+ 在总参数量不变时使用独立层级编码器以减少编码计算。三个数据集和三种 tokenizer 的实验支持其推荐效果及 LESSRec+ 的计算收益。

original_abstract.text: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.
original_abstract.source_title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations

en.text: EmbeddingGemma 2 places text, images, audio, video and mixed inputs in one embedding space. Simplified per-layer embeddings and a staged modality/objective curriculum support quality across modalities. The reported benchmarks outperform specialist and 2–12x larger models; selective encoder loading, adjustable visual-token budgets, truncatable dimensions and quantized weights provide deployment tradeoffs.

zh.text: EmbeddingGemma 2把文本、图像、音频、视频及混合输入映射到同一表征空间，通过简化逐层embedding和分阶段模态／目标课程训练提升跨模态质量。论文报告在所测基准中超过专用模型及规模大2至12倍的模型，并提供按需加载模态编码器、调整视觉token预算、截断向量维度和权重量化等部署选项。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. Because most intermediate channels in a routed expert contribute little to any single token, channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. We show that channel selection needs no calibration data. First, a calibrated threshold does not fix how much a selector reads, because the number of channels passing it varies across inputs; Prox with thresholds calibrated for an 18% read budget actually reads only 12.9% on average across our benchmarks. Second, top-k keeps each token's k highest-scoring channels and needs no calibration data. At the calibrated budget, a selector's top-k version matches or beats its threshold version on the same score in 40 of 43 comparisons at 13% and 18% budgets, including all 23 on generation tasks. The top-k versions also avoid the repetition-loop collapse that calibrated thresholds cause on Gemma 4. Calibrating a threshold thus provides neither of the two things selectors use it for: a known read budget and a consistent accuracy gain at that budget. We furthermore introduce a reader built entirely from the model's weights, which screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers the skipped ones with a low-rank map. Across three post-trained MoE models, our reader retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads, with Triton kernels running MoE blocks 1.60 to 1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches on the same three models.
original_abstract.source_title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data

en.text: The paper replaces calibrated channel-selection thresholds with per-token top-k selection for predictable routed-expert read budgets. It also builds a weight-only reader using a ternary sketch and low-rank recovery of skipped channels. Across three post-trained MoE models, the reader retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of expert-weight reads; Triton MoE blocks run 1.60–1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one, and up to 2.69x at larger batches.

zh.text: 论文以逐 token 的 top-k 通道选择替代依赖校准数据的阈值，固定路由专家的读取预算，并提出仅依据模型权重、结合三值草图与低秩补偿的读取器。在三个后训练 MoE 模型上，以 17.8% 的专家权重读取保留全模型 98.1% 的准确率；Triton MoE 模块在批量为一时相对优化后的 vLLM 加速 1.60–1.90 倍，在较大批量时最高 2.69 倍。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained edge platforms is often dominated by expert-weight movement rather than computation. Although each token activates only a small subset of experts, routing is input-dependent, so all experts must remain accessible and memory movement dominates latency. Existing approaches such as uniform pruning and expert dropping overlook two properties of MoE execution: expert combinations are highly skewed in frequency, and experts contribute asymmetrically within each combination. We present CRISP, a combination-aware framework that co-designs pruning and runtime scheduling for efficient MoE serving on memory-constrained edge platforms. CRISP reorders neurons by importance so one stored expert can support multiple execution widths, assigns differentiated execution to hot, warm, and cold combinations based on frequency and expert role, and exploits heterogeneous widths to overlap expert loading with computation. Across Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, CRISP improves throughput by up to $2.1\times$ at the same memory budget while limiting accuracy loss to 3.6\% relative to full-width inference. Our results highlight that efficient edge MoE serving requires jointly optimizing which expert capacity is preserved and how expert execution is scheduled.
original_abstract.source_title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers

en.text: CRISP jointly designs expert pruning and runtime scheduling for memory-constrained MoE inference. Neuron reordering lets one stored expert execute at several widths; expert-combination frequency and each expert's role determine how much computation to retain, while heterogeneous widths help overlap weight loading with computation. On Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, it reports up to 2.1 times throughput at the same memory budget, with reported accuracy loss limited to 3.6% relative to full-width inference. The result informs sparse-model deployment with an explicit quality trade-off rather than demonstrating CTR gains.

zh.text: CRISP 联合设计显存受限 MoE 推理的剪枝与调度。它先按重要性重排神经元，让同一份专家权重支持不同执行宽度，再根据专家组合出现频率及各专家的作用分配计算，并利用不同宽度把权重加载与计算重叠。在 Mixtral-8x7B 和 DeepSeek-MoE-16B 上，论文报告同等内存预算下吞吐最高达到 2.1 倍，相对全宽度推理的准确率损失控制在所报的 3.6% 范围内。这是带有效果折损的稀疏模型部署方案，未验证 CTR 收益。

original_abstract.text: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. We further develop a theoretical framework for hierarchical preference decomposition over the SID prefix tree, proving an exact factorization of collaborative preference distributions and a weighted decomposition of item-level KL divergence into prefix-conditional KL divergences. Building on this analysis, we distill a discriminative teacher's full conditional distributions over all legal next tokens at ground-truth prefixes along the target SID path, jointly optimizing this objective with cross-entropy. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over existing GR baselines and support the effectiveness of the proposed preference distillation.
original_abstract.source_title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation

en.text: REGER explicitly models inter-item relations through semantic-neighbor SID pretraining, combined global and SID-boundary local attention, and discriminative-teacher preference distillation. A hierarchical SID-prefix analysis factorizes collaborative preferences and item-level KL divergence, motivating distillation over all legal next tokens along target prefixes. Experiments on real-world datasets report consistent gains over generative-recommendation baselines.

zh.text: REGER 通过语义邻居 SID 预训练、全局与 SID 边界局部注意力结合，以及判别式教师偏好蒸馏，显式建模物品间关系。对 SID 前缀树的层级分析分解协同偏好及物品级 KL 散度，据此在目标前缀上蒸馏全部合法下一 token 的分布。真实数据集实验报告持续优于生成式推荐基线。

original_abstract.text: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.
original_abstract.source_title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing

en.text: MERLIN improves multi-state linear attention by tracking first and second moments of segment keys, allowing queries to use both mean and variance of alignment when combining memory-state readouts. Tests on Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M report stronger long-context retrieval and question answering, including improvements over baselines using four times more memory. The method offers a general content-aware routing design for compressed sequence states.

zh.text: MERLIN 跟踪各片段键向量的一阶与二阶矩，使查询在聚合多状态线性注意力输出时同时利用对齐均值和方差。在 Gated DeltaNet-1.3B 与 Mamba-2-780M 上，实验报告长上下文检索和问答改进，甚至超过使用四倍内存的基线，为压缩序列状态提供通用的内容感知路由设计。

original_abstract.text: Spectral compression reduces the storage and scoring costs of dense retrieval by projecting embeddings onto a smaller principal subspace. However, its corpus-derived weighting rules tie all retained directions to a shared spectral trend, without directly accounting for their individual contributions to relevance. To address this, we propose Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration (RRC), a closed-form method for refining spectral weights using relevance judgments. RRC estimates margin-based weights from the means and variances of positive--negative score contributions along each retained direction. It retains directions with positive estimated weights, decomposes their log weights into a fitted power-law trend and a residual, and adds the residual to the compressor's log weights on this support. This allows relevance judgments to adjust individual directions while preserving the compressor's overall spectral trend. RRC applies to PCA, Whitening, and SpecTemp, and incorporates the corrections into the existing transformation shared by documents and queries, without iterative model training or an additional inference stage. Experiments with three encoders on nine datasets covering conventional and reasoning-intensive retrieval show that SpecTemp + RRC achieves the highest mean effectiveness among tested compressors on the BEIR group and BRIGHT at every target dimension. On the five evaluated BRIGHT datasets, it improves over SpecTemp by an average of 2.34 nDCG@10 points at 768 dimensions. The gains also persist under scalar and product quantization, improving the trade-off between per-document storage and retrieval effectiveness. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/rrc-spectral-compression-B5CE/
original_abstract.source_title: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings

en.text: RRC uses relevance judgments to calibrate individual spectral-compression directions while preserving the compressor’s overall spectral trend. Its closed-form residual correction is folded into the existing query–document transformation, requiring neither iterative training nor an extra inference stage. Across three encoders and nine retrieval datasets, SpecTemp + RRC achieves the best mean effectiveness among tested compressors at every evaluated target dimension; on five BRIGHT datasets, the average gain is 2.34 nDCG@10 points at 768 dimensions. Gains also persist with scalar and product quantization, informing storage-efficient retrieval embeddings.

zh.text: RRC 用相关性标注调整谱压缩中各方向的权重，同时保留压缩器整体的谱趋势。闭式计算得到的残差修正直接并入查询与文档已有的变换，不需要迭代训练或额外推理阶段。在三个编码器、九个检索数据集的实验中，SpecTemp + RRC 在各测试目标维度上取得被比较压缩器中的最佳平均效果；五个 BRIGHT 数据集在 768 维时平均提升 2.34 个 nDCG@10 点。收益在标量和乘积量化后仍保留，可用于检索向量存储成本与效果的权衡。

original_abstract.text: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload. During forward execution, it plans retention quotas and expert placement under resource constraints while preserving all routed computations. During backpropagation, a load recalibration metric estimates each token-expert pair's contribution to the expert update and selects pairs within these quotas. A capacity-aware routing algorithm distributes retained pairs among eligible instances of their original experts. Physical compaction then forms smaller communication payloads and variable-size grouped GEMMs, reducing backward traffic, computation, and execution-buffer demand. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B show that LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.
original_abstract.source_title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes

en.text: LRMoE reduces memory-constrained MoE training cost by jointly setting expert-placement and backward-retention quotas. It preserves all routed forward computations, then selects token-expert pairs for backpropagation according to estimated update contribution and routes retained pairs to instances of their original experts. Compact communication buffers and variable-size grouped matrix multiplications reduce backward work. On Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B, cumulative MoE-layer time to fixed-loss targets falls by 21.2–44.8% versus SYMI, providing a systems reference for sparse scaling rather than a demonstrated recommendation gain.

zh.text: LRMoE 联合规划专家放置和反向计算保留配额，降低显存受限节点上的 MoE 训练成本。它保留全部已路由的前向计算，反向传播时按估计的参数更新贡献筛选 token—专家对，再将保留的计算分配给原专家的可用实例。通过压紧通信缓冲区和使用可变大小的分组矩阵乘法，减少反向计算与通信。在 Qwen3-30B-A3B 和 GLM4.5-106B-A12B 上，达到固定损失目标所需的累计 MoE 层训练时间相对 SYMI 减少 21.2–44.8%。这为稀疏扩展提供了系统层参考，并非已验证的推荐收益。

original_abstract.text: As growing compute budgets outpace the growth of high-quality training data, large language models must be trained with both compute and data constraints in mind. Unfortunately, existing prescriptions for data-constrained scaling suffer from two important limitations. First, past works hold key hyperparameters such as weight decay fixed with scale, despite the fact that optimal hyperparameters vary wildly with model size and number of epochs. Second, past works neglect ensembling, a promising axis for scaling under data constraints. As a surprising consequence, prior prescriptions can lead to loss that increases with compute budget. We address both limitations by fitting power laws that prescribe how to transfer hyperparameters with scale and scaling laws that prescribe how to allocate compute with ensembling. Training on 100M tokens from FineWeb, our recipe reduces validation loss by over 0.15 nats compared to prior recipes, a 14% decrease in perplexity, and achieves monotonic improvements with compute through ensembling. These gains are achieved using prescriptions fit to smaller runs and validated at up to 12$\times$ larger compute budgets.
original_abstract.source_title: Improving Data-Constrained Scaling with Hyperparameter Transfer and Ensembling

en.text: This work improves data-constrained language-model scaling by fitting power laws for hyperparameter transfer and scaling laws for allocating compute to ensembles. On 100M FineWeb training tokens, the recipe reduces validation loss by over 0.15 nats, or perplexity by 14%, relative to prior recipes, and reports monotonic improvements with compute through ensembling. Prescriptions fitted to smaller runs are validated at up to 12-fold larger compute budgets. The method may inform data-limited ranking experiments, but transfer to CTR models and ensemble serving costs remain unverified here.

zh.text: 这项工作针对训练数据受限时的模型扩展，拟合超参数随规模迁移的幂律，并用 scaling law 分配集成模型的计算预算。在 FineWeb 的 1 亿训练 token 上，相比既有方案，验证损失降低超过 0.15 nats、困惑度降低 14%，且集成方案随计算预算增加持续改善。由小规模实验拟合的配置在最高 12 倍计算预算下得到验证。其方法可供数据受限的排序实验参考，但摘要未验证 CTR 迁移效果或集成模型的线上服务成本。

original_abstract.text: Many open mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models train with Muon instead of AdamW. Most balance the load with a bias on each expert's routing score, adjusted after every step. Their recipes disagree on whether Muon should also train the router. In models with 55M and 108M active parameters, we measure how the optimizer changes the span of these biases, the largest minus the smallest in a layer. The span grows when all tokens favor the same experts, so it shows how hard a layer is to balance. At learning rates tuned on shorter runs, Muon raised the span of the first MoE layer at every seed, roughly doubling it on average, while the other layers changed much less. The rise came from Muon on the rest of the network, whichever optimizer trained the router. In those runs, the inputs to the first router shared a direction, and soon after the warmup its busiest expert averaged four to seven times its fair share. Over the first 3,000 steps, subtracting the batch mean from these inputs removed this overload while barely changing the loss. On the smaller model, halving Muon's learning rate removed most of the rise and slightly improved the loss. Moving only the router to AdamW made the loads shift more during the warmup and slightly raised the loss, so at this scale the results favor keeping the router on Muon.
original_abstract.source_title: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance

en.text: In MoE language models with 55M and 108M active parameters, this study finds that Muon can increase load imbalance in the first expert layer even when its router uses a different optimizer. Shared directions in router inputs coincide with expert overload; subtracting the batch mean removes the observed early overload with little loss change, while reducing Muon's learning rate helps on the smaller model. The findings inform optimizer and routing diagnostics for sparse scaling, but their demonstrated scope is limited to these model sizes and training settings.

zh.text: 这项研究在激活参数为 5500 万和 1.08 亿的 MoE 语言模型中发现，Muon 会加重第一层专家的负载不均，即使单独更换路由器优化器也不能消除这一现象。路由输入中的共同方向伴随专家过载；减去批次均值可消除观察到的早期过载，损失变化很小，在较小模型上降低 Muon 学习率也有帮助。这为稀疏扩展中的优化器选择和路由诊断提供参考，结论范围限于论文测试的模型规模和训练设定。

original_abstract.text: LLM-based generative recommendation reads long, text-rich interaction histories but generates only short semantic identifiers (SIDs). This asymmetry makes supervised fine-tuning inefficient: encoding the history is expensive, yet each history usually provides supervision for only one target. We present Merge and Branch (M&B) to reduce input cost and learn more from each encoded history. Merge compresses each historical item's SID and text into a small number of learned tokens. Branch uses the compressed history to predict multiple target SIDs. To share history computation while keeping these targets independent, M&B organizes each example as a shallow, wide tree. We develop tree FlashAttention to execute this layout efficiently, processing the shared history once and propagating gradients from every branch for end-to-end training. A tree-structured key/value cache extends history sharing to constrained decoding. Experiments on public benchmarks show that M&B outperforms strong recommendation baselines while substantially improving training and decoding efficiency. Online A/B tests on a large-scale e-commerce platform suggest that M&B effectively combines item text with multi-target supervision, yielding statistically significant gains in per-user clicks, orders, and GMV.
original_abstract.source_title: Merge and Branch: Efficient Tree-Structured Supervised Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Recommendation

en.text: Merge and Branch reduces the cost of supervised fine-tuning for generative recommendation by compressing each historical item’s semantic ID and text into learned tokens, then predicting multiple independent target IDs from the shared history. Tree FlashAttention and a tree-structured key/value cache reuse history computation during training and constrained decoding. Public benchmarks report improved recommendation quality and training and decoding efficiency. Newly reported online A/B tests on a large e-commerce platform show statistically significant gains in per-user clicks, orders and GMV, without specifying their magnitudes. The design makes one history encoding support multiple supervision targets.

zh.text: Merge and Branch先把历史物品的语义ID与文本压成少量可学习token，再用同一段历史独立预测多个目标ID。树状FlashAttention让各目标分支共享历史计算，树状KV缓存把复用延伸到约束解码。公开基准报告推荐效果及训练、解码效率改善；新版摘要还加入大型电商平台A/B测试，人均点击、订单和GMV均有统计显著提升，但未披露幅度。可借鉴的是用一次历史编码承担多个目标的监督与预测。

original_abstract.text: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Super and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, open and efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer models designed for reasoning, long-context understanding, and agentic workloads. Super is a 120B-parameter, 12B-active multimodal model, while Lightning is a smaller 30B-parameter, 3B-active text model; both designed for efficient deployment. Both models combine large-scale distillation, long-context training, and native speculative decoding, while Super further incorporates Indic continued pretraining and agentic software-engineering mid-training. We develop a comprehensive post-training pipeline spanning supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RLVR and RLHF), complemented in Super by specialized teacher training and multi- teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). This transforms Super from a text-only base model into a multimodal agent capable of reasoning over text, images, video, and interactive tool environments. We further explore test-time scaling through parallel agent execution and self-verification. Across training and deployment, we jointly optimize capability and efficiency. Indic continued pretraining improves Indian-language benchmarks by up to 9.82 percentage points, while agentic mid-training strengthens software-engineering capabilities and robustness across agent harnesses. The post-trained Super model achieves 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro, surpassing Nemotron 3 Ultra despite using approximately 4.6x fewer active parameters. Post-training MTP boosting improves speculative- decoding acceptance length by up to 21.8% under probabilistic draft sampling, while NVFP4 quantization achieves 99.62% median accuracy recovery relative to BF16. Inference optimizations enable up to 4,856 output tokens/s/GPU on GB200 while sustaining at least 50 tokens/s/user.
original_abstract.source_title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI

zh.text: 报告120B总参数、12B激活参数的Super与30B总参数、3B激活参数的Lightning，结合Mamba-Transformer混合架构、MoE、蒸馏和原生推测解码。NVFP4量化的准确率恢复中位数达到BF16的99.62%，展示稀疏架构、缓存管理与部署精度协同优化的工程路径。

en.text: Presents the 120B/12B-active Super and 30B/3B-active Lightning hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE models, combining distillation, long-context training and native speculative decoding. NVFP4 quantization reports 99.62% median accuracy recovery relative to BF16. The report provides engineering recipes connecting sparse architecture, cache management and deployment precision.

original_abstract.text: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) is now a common ingredient in language-model pre-training, as it improves downstream performance and enables faster inference through speculative decoding. We identify a flaw in standard MTP training, in which a residual component of the MTP gradient interferes with both next-token and multi-token learning, increasingly so with scale. Specifically, the MTP cross-entropy gradient can be decomposed exactly into a KL self-distillation term that pulls each MTP head toward the model's own next-token prediction (NTP) distribution and improves speculative decoding, and a residual that has a low signal-to-noise ratio and buries the useful KL signal. We introduce the KL gradient-recovery trick: when two distributions share a linear output head, the gradient of their KL divergence can be recovered exactly by combining their cross-entropy gradients through straight-through gradient routing. Unlike minimizing the KL directly, this trick requires no vocabulary-sized logit matrices and is compatible with standard fused cross-entropy kernels. This enables Soft Multi-Token Prediction (Soft-MTP), a one-line code change to MTP that removes the noisy residual and backpropagates only the KL self-distillation signal by reusing the existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy computations. Soft-MTP supports both DeepSeek- and Meta-style MTP, adds no parameters, and incurs no measurable overhead. From 167M to 1.2B parameters, Soft-MTP improves over standard MTP with lower NTP perplexity, faster speculative decoding and higher zero-shot accuracy at every scale, lower MTP perplexity from 689M onward, and stronger math and code reasoning after fine-tuning at 1.2B. Soft-MTP also matches, if not exceeds, direct KL divergence minimization on most metrics. Soft-MTP is, in effect, a free lunch for MTP optimization. Our code can be found at https://github.com/JaydenTeoh/Soft-MTP.
original_abstract.source_title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right

en.text: Soft-MTP separates a useful KL self-distillation gradient from a noisy residual in multi-token prediction. Straight-through routing recovers the KL gradient from existing cross-entropy computations without vocabulary-sized logit matrices; 167M–1.2B language-model experiments report improved next-token perplexity, speculative decoding and zero-shot accuracy over standard MTP.

zh.text: Soft-MTP从多token预测梯度中分离有用的KL自蒸馏项和噪声残差。直通梯度路由复用已有交叉熵计算恢复KL梯度，无需保存词表大小的logit矩阵；1.67亿至12亿参数语言模型实验中，下一token困惑度、推测解码和零样本准确率均优于标准MTP。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation (GR) reformulates item retrieval as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs), offering a unified paradigm for personalized recommendation. GR4AD, as an industrial generative recommendation framework, has greatly improved advertising revenue while enabling efficient real-time serving in Kuaishou.However, continued deployment has exposed three limitations: deterministic SID assignment remains sensitive to semantic boundaries; conventional backbone scaling provides diminishing revenue gains under strict serving constraints; and sequence-level value optimization provides limited credit assignment to intermediate SID decisions, causing likelihood-based beam search to prematurely prune potentially high-value candidates. We present GR4AD-X, which addresses these limitations through reliable SID construction, serving-efficient capacity scaling, and unified value alignment. Specifically, GR4AD-X improves SID reliability through Multi-Path assignment. It expands model capacity along multiple complementary dimensions rather than relying solely on wider or deeper backbones, achieving a better effectiveness-efficiency trade-off under strict serving constraints. Finally, Unified Value-Guided Generation and Discrimination (UniVGD) aligns generation with commercial value through prefix-level reward optimization, value-guided beam pruning, and discriminative reranking within a unified model. Large-scale online A/B tests on the Kuaishou advertising platform demonstrate that GR4AD-X achieves a cumulative revenue improvement of 3.07% over the deployed GR4AD baseline while satisfying strict latency and throughput constraints.
original_abstract.source_title: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising

en.text: GR4AD-X combines multi-path semantic-ID assignment, capacity expansion across complementary dimensions, and unified value-guided generation and reranking for advertising retrieval under serving constraints. Prefix-level rewards and value-guided beam pruning aim to retain commercially valuable candidates. Online A/B tests on Kuaishou report a cumulative 3.07% revenue improvement over deployed GR4AD while meeting latency and throughput constraints, offering a serving-aware approach to generative-recommendation scaling.

zh.text: GR4AD-X 面向受延迟和吞吐约束的广告生成式召回，结合多路径语义 ID 分配、多维容量扩展，以及统一的价值引导生成与重排。它用前缀级奖励和价值引导的束搜索剪枝，减少高商业价值候选被过早丢弃。快手线上 A/B 实验报告，相对已部署 GR4AD 累计收入提升 3.07%，同时满足服务约束，为生成式推荐的扩容与线上成本协同设计提供参考。

original_abstract.text: Repeating transformer layers can improve language model performance without adding parameters. However, the added computational depth increases both forward and backward computation costs during training. Training such models requires choosing a backward window that controls how many final layer repetitions retain gradients during backpropagation. Longer windows improve per-token learning efficiency but increase per-update cost, while shorter windows reduce per-update cost but sacrifice per-token efficiency. Understanding which window performs better requires examining different training budgets. Prior work compares backward windows across computational budgets. When training budgets increase, it remains unclear whether the same window continues to perform best. We measure how the relative performance of two windows shifts as training budgets grow. Our method isolates per-token efficiency by training both windows on identical data, and compares complete training recipes at approximately equal training time at each budget. Results show that shorter windows lose much of their advantage as budgets grow. Controlled experiments show that both benefits decrease at larger budgets, with a greater decline in the benefit of extended training. Backward window comparisons depend on the available budget, and the preferred window among the tested candidates can change as the budget grows.
original_abstract.source_title: Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets

en.text: This study compares how many final repetitions of a looped language model should retain gradients during training. Identical-data experiments isolate learning efficiency per token, while approximately time-matched recipes compare the trade-off between deeper backpropagation and more updates. The tested shorter window loses much of its advantage as training budgets grow, so the preferred choice can change with budget. This offers a budget-aware training lesson for weight-sharing depth architectures; it does not establish a universal optimal window or a CTR result.

zh.text: 这项研究比较循环语言模型训练时，应让最后多少轮层重复保留梯度。相同数据实验用于分离每 token 的学习效率，近似等训练时间实验则比较更深反向传播与更多参数更新的取舍。结果显示，预算增加后，所测试短窗口的优势明显减弱，较优窗口可能随预算变化。可借鉴的是共享权重深度架构的训练配置应随预算评估；论文未给出普遍最优窗口或 CTR 结果。
